blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — guaifenesin therapeutic purpose
stem: A client with a productive cough asks what guaifenesin is intended to do. Which response is correct?

options.A: It acts as an expectorant that loosens phlegm and thins bronchial secretions, helping make the cough more productive.
options.B: It acts as a cough suppressant that reduces the central cough reflex, helping decrease the frequency of productive coughing.
options.C: It acts as a bronchodilator that relaxes airway smooth muscle, helping relieve bronchospasm associated with the productive cough.
options.D: It acts as an antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors, helping reduce allergic upper-airway secretions and sneezing.

rationale: Current OTC guaifenesin labeling identifies guaifenesin as an expectorant and states that it helps loosen phlegm and thin bronchial secretions to make coughs more productive. Therefore A correctly describes the labeled therapeutic purpose. B describes a centrally acting antitussive effect, C describes bronchodilation, and D describes H1-antihistamine activity; none is the labeled purpose of guaifenesin.
educational_objective: Explain that guaifenesin is an expectorant used to loosen phlegm and thin bronchial secretions so a cough can be more productive.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA OTC labeling
source_version_date: DailyMed updated June 18, 2026; version 11 published July 1, 2026 (current); accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Drug Facts — Purpose: Expectorant; Uses: helps loosen phlegm (mucus) and thin bronchial secretions to make coughs more productive.
source_claim_supported: Guaifenesin is an expectorant that helps loosen phlegm and thin bronchial secretions to make coughs more productive.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: educate client about medications; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; evaluate client response to medication.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as substantive medication-purpose statements without absolute-word distractor cues.
Length-balanced the options and replaced implausible distractors with recognizable but incorrect pharmacologic mechanisms.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current OTC guaifenesin Purpose and Uses language. B–D are plausible drug-class mechanisms but not guaifenesin's labeled therapeutic purpose, and the original cueing pattern is removed.
